# `set_view_plan_target_name`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the target name that the device uses for the current view and for autosaved captures.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; absent from the 32-bit build) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xdee90, SetViewTargetName @0x3c0fd0 (64-bit build only) |

Only on device process type 2. An empty target_name clears the stored view target name. A non-empty name is regularised as a filename, stored as the view target info, then copied (name and coordinates) to the global autosave settings. The inspected helper does not clear a pending match from iscope_match_target_name. The helper's return value is ignored, so no downstream error is reported. Registered in the 64-bit build only.

Side effects: Changes the stored view target name and the global autosave target used to name captures. No worker is launched. No explicit timeout.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_view_plan_target_name"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Object required (no positional form). Unknown members are ignored. [READ] |
| `params.target_name` | string | yes | - | New target name. The empty string is accepted and clears the stored name. A non-empty name is passed through the device's filename regulariser before it is stored; the stored form can therefore differ from the one sent. Missing, null or non-string is rejected with 105. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 210 | Device process type is not 2 | `not supported` |
| 107 | params absent or not an object | `expected object param` |
| 105 | target_name missing, null or not a string | `expected string param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":70,"method":"set_view_plan_target_name","params":{"target_name":"Example target"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"method":"set_view_plan_target_name","result":0,"code":0,"id":70}
```

Reply, bad-name:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_view_plan_target_name","error":"expected string param","code":105,"id":71}
```
